items.text: I was proud to announce an additional $1.27M in funding for the Twentynine Palms wastewater treatment project has been secured through the House at a recent meeting with Mayor O’Gilvie. These projects are critical to enabling community growth & protecting groundwater resources. https://t.co/2IsMBfPQbl

Quality specialized health care can be hard to come by in our rural area, with many patients driving over an hour to seek treatment. I toured Hi-Desert Dialysis recently to see the facility and discuss how we can meet our community’s unique health care needs. https://t.co/zUsXZdrBay

Virtual health is a critical to combating drug addiction in rural communities like #CA23 where treatment facilities & medical care can be far from home. Thank you to our witnesses at @HouseCommerce's recent Health Subcommittee hearing for their testimony on this critical issue. https://t.co/fd3P4Ws2Pm

The House recently passed the Lower Costs, More Transparency Act, delivering legislation that will lower health care costs and increase price transparency for patients. I was proud to support this legislation as a key step in helping to address our unaffordable health care system. https://t.co/RCiI6o7bZa

Some federal health care programs use Quality-Adjusted Life Years (QALYs) to evaluate the cost effectiveness of potential treatment options. I voted for H.R. 485 to ban QALYs because I believe strongly that the government should not be discriminating against people with disabilities.
https://t.co/aJJXyvXAKp

The medical personnel at our local hospitals and medical centers deserve our gratitude for keeping our community healthy. This week I visited the Arrowhead Regional Medical Center to discuss how we can better support our doctors, nurses, and the patients who rely on these facilities for their care.

Innovations in healthcare technology, such as virtual health, are delivering better health outcomes for patients and expanding access to underserved, rural communities like those in #CA23. I enjoyed meeting with Southern California Permanente Medical Group this week to discuss how we can continue to expand virtual health services in our rural communities.

Over the last three decades, access to versatile and innovative treatment options for Type 1 Diabetes has drastically improved due to the funding of the Special Diabetes Program by Congress. I enjoyed meeting with representatives from Breakthrough T1D’s Southern California Chapter for an update on ways we are treating – and hopefully one day curing – Type 1 Diabetes.

Improving access to affordable healthcare in #CA23 is one of my top priorities. That’s why I held a roundtable recently with local healthcare service providers to discuss the challenges facing patients and providers in our community. https://t.co/zZC57cWvv6

Closing the digital divide is one of my top priorities in Congress, which is why I toured a communications tower site to see how broadband infrastructure is being deployed in #CA23. We must continue to extend broadband coverage in rural areas like ours. https://t.co/b1Vx7UXb8L

As we come to the end of Breast Cancer Awareness Month, I was proud to support the SCREENS for Cancer Act when it passed through the House Energy and Commerce Committee. We must continue to support screening, diagnostic, and treatment services for those in our community that lack access to these lifesaving services.

Medicare open enrollment ends December 7th, meaning that time is running out for you to change your Medicare health and coverage plans. If you’re satisfied with your current Medicare plan and it is still offered, you don’t need to change your plan. If not, you must make your choice by December 7th. If you need more information on the process, please reach out to my District office at (760) 247-1815.

The Constitutional Concealed Carry Reciprocity Act ensures that law-abiding citizens can exercise their Second Amendment rights across state lines. This bill provides a clear framework for concealed carry reciprocity while respecting state laws. I am a proud cosponsor of this legislation that supports freedom and self-defense for law-abiding Americans.

I am reintroducing critical legislation to strengthen the 988 Suicide and Crisis Lifeline against cyberattacks. Protecting this critical resource ensures in remains resilient, accessible, and reliable – preventing shutdowns that could cost lives. Mental health support must always be secure. https://t.co/v6JghVqXBN

I recently introduced the Medical Device Electronic Labeling Act, a commonsense bill to modernize medical device labeling and eliminate unnecessary costs. By allowing more devices to use electronic labeling, we can streamline access to critical information for healthcare providers while reducing waste. This is a simple change that supports innovation and efficiency in our healthcare system.

This week I hosted a virtual town hall focused on the issues that matter most to seniors in California’s 23rd District—protecting Social Security and Medicare, improving veterans' care, and strengthening our economy. Thank you to the thousands who joined me and asked thoughtful questions. I’ll always fight to protect the benefits you’ve earned and ensure your voice is heard in Washington.

April is Cancer Prevention and Early Detection month, a time to promote research that reduces the risk of cancer while also taking steps to advance cancer treatment. Every step counts in the fight against cancer! https://t.co/RkqDW6yzk7

The SUPPORT for Patients and Communities Act has passed the Energy and Commerce Committee! I’m especially proud it includes my bill, the 9-8-8 Lifeline Cybersecurity Responsibility Act. Strengthening the cybersecurity of the 9-8-8 Suicide and Crisis Lifeline is essential to ensuring Americans have uninterrupted access to lifesaving mental health support.

Melanie from Redlands applied for Social Security and Medicare in January but didn’t hear back for months. After she contacted my office, we were able to quickly resolve her problem. If you need help with a federal agency, stop by one of our mobile office hours or visit our main district office in Hesperia. We’re here to serve you

Medicaid is on an unsustainable trajectory. Today, I supported legislation to strengthen Medicaid and ensure it’s there for the people who depend on it- children, pregnant women, individuals with disabilities, and seniors. We're securing the future of the program by increasing accountability so it can continue to serve as a critical safety net for our fellow Americans for years to come.

I enjoyed connecting with Twentynine Palms Councilmember April Ramirez to discuss expanding healthcare access for veterans in rural areas. We're working on solutions such as mobile medical services to better serve communities like Twentynine Palms. https://t.co/RcfdsnLmkf

The unauthorized sharing of private health data—including pregnancy status, prescriptions, and Social Security information—with third-party advertisers is deeply troubling. That’s why I joined Rep. Guthrie in demanding answers from Covered California. Californians deserve accountability and transparency when their privacy is compromised.

The US spends between two and three times more per capita on healthcare than other developed countries do on healthcare and achieves worse health outcomes. I questioned @SecKennedy about how artificial intelligence might radically improve healthcare in the United States. It’s time we harness the power of AI to revolutionize patient care and streamline provider efficiency.

I proudly voted for the FY26 MilCon-VA Appropriations Act which fully funds veterans’ health care, supports military families, and strengthens our national defense. This bill reflects our commitment to those who’ve served, protects American values, and keeps our promises to those who put on the uniform of our country.

The passage of H.R. 1 marks a major win for the American people. This legislation cuts taxes for working families, secures our southern border, strengthens Medicaid for those who depend on it, and reins in wasteful Washington spending—all without raising taxes. I proudly supported this bill because it will meaningfully improve quality of life for the people in our district.
